definition: The EuroMatrixPlus is a project that ran from March 2009 to February 2012.
details: EuroMatrixPlus succeeded a project called EuroMatrix (September 2006 to February 2009) and continued in further development and improvement of machine translation (MT) systems for languages of the European Union (EU).

explainer.lead: EuroMatrixPlus was a project that continued earlier work on machine translation for European Union languages. Running from March 2009 to February 2012, it focused on developing and improving translation systems rather than starting from scratch.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a team teaching computers to translate between languages, then passing its work to another team to make it better. EuroMatrixPlus was that second team’s project, following EuroMatrix and working on translations involving European Union languages. It ran from March 2009 until February 2012.
tiers.practitioner: Treat EuroMatrixPlus as a project identifier and historical context, not as a specific algorithm or software package. When examining EU-language machine translation work from 2009–2012, distinguish it from the predecessor EuroMatrix project and identify the particular system or method involved before applying anything in practice.
tiers.paperLevel: EuroMatrixPlus was the successor to EuroMatrix, which ran from September 2006 to February 2009. EuroMatrixPlus ran from March 2009 to February 2012, with its scope defined as the further development and improvement of machine translation systems for European Union languages.

explainer.example: Consider a team improving an English–Czech machine translation system during this period. That illustrates the kind of EU-language system development and improvement within EuroMatrixPlus’s scope, under the project running from March 2009 to February 2012.

explainer.intuition: Improving machine translation is a continuing process: one project can build a foundation, and a successor can refine the systems and extend the work. EuroMatrixPlus played that successor role for EU-language machine translation.
howItWorks: EuroMatrix carried out the earlier project phase from September 2006 to February 2009.
The new project continued developing and improving machine translation systems.
Its language focus was the languages of the European Union.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provided continuity after EuroMatrix, keeping the improvement of machine translation systems for European Union languages moving through February 2012.
misconceptions: EuroMatrixPlus was not the original EuroMatrix project; it was the successor.
It was a time-bounded project, not an ongoing programme, and ended in February 2012.
The project name does not by itself identify a particular translation algorithm.
